Daily Devotional

November 9

15 Let us therefore, as many as be perfect, be thus minded: and if in any thing ye be otherwise minded, God shall reveal even this unto you. (Philippians 3:15 KJV)

Paul was not saying we need to be without fault when he said perfect, but he is saying that we need to be spiritually mature, and that is what the word meant. The like minded is referring to us being stayed with our minds upon Christ at all times, otherwise seeking God with all our efforts, and keeping our minds focused on the things of God. None of us will ever be perfect in the sense of not having any faults or failures (Romans 3:23), but we can be mature Christians, and seek God with our whole mind. The mature Christian is one who has stayed in the Word of God and renewed their mind, as the bible teaches (Romans 12:2). This has nothing to do with age, but with maturity in the knowledge of God. We need to all renew our minds by seeking God with all our hearts.

This is a wonderful promise, that if we will seek the Lord with all our heart, then He will let us know when we start to stray away from Him. This is our assurance that He will continue to guide us in our effort to follow Him, and will keep us focused upon Him at all times. Many Christians have wondered how they would know if they begin to stray from following God and this tells us that He will help us keep on track. God is so good, and He is always there for us, as He promises to never leave us nor forsake us (Hebrews 13:5), and He loves us unconditionally, so He will guide us as any loving Father would do. It is all about getting to know God in an intimate way (John 17:3), and that was the purpose of sending His Son, to bring us back into this kind of relationship. Thank you Lord for being our loving Father and guiding us in this life.

Devotional by Pastor Joe W. Green, www.Infinite-Faith.com
